reason: The text of Exodus fundamentally contradicts this statement. Throughout the narrative, God consistently sides with the oppressed common people (Israelites) against the elite (Pharaoh and Egyptian rulers), delivering the enslaved through miraculous intervention and striking down the elite through plagues as divine judgment. In Exodus 18, when establishing judicial governance, the text explicitly prescribes selecting leaders based on moral character—'men of valor, fear-fearing, truthful, hating bribery'—not inherent superiority. The narrative arc portrays liberation from oppressive hierarchy, demonstrating that worth and leadership capability derive from virtue and God's calling, not from elite status. The text consistently elevates the common people as worthy of divine protection and direct covenantal relationship.
